title: Canonical lepton-mass-tower factor ξ_m = [2m-1]_q · [m]_q / [2m]_q: matches muon (m=2 → [3]_q·[2]_q/[4]_q, 0.001%) and tau (m=3 → [5]_q·[3]_q/[6]_q, +0.79%) of CODATA. Supersedes the earlier muon-only d_q(std_rep S_{n+1})·[2]_q/[n+1]_q reading (whose tau prediction was falsified); categorical derivation of the q-bracket form remains open.
html:
Conjecture (lepton-tower closure factor). Let K_\ell be the canonical knot for the lepton at tower-index m (electron m=1, muon m=2, tau m=3). The canonical mass-tower correction factor is

  \xi_m \;=\; \frac{[2m-1]_q \cdot [m]_q}{[2m]_q}.

The factor (2m-1, m, 2m) exhibits strict symmetry in h = q - q^{-1}. The odd upper index contributes a bar-anti-symmetric upper-jet bracket. The even lower index contributes a bar-symmetric closing trace. This precise amphichiral reflection reflects the knot-operator equivalence structural directive.

The predicted muon factor [3]_q \cdot [2]_q / [4]_q matches the empirical requirement to within 0.001\%. The tau factor [5]_q \cdot [3]_q / [6]_q matches to within 0.79\%. The full categorical derivation of this branching factor from the H_{2m+1} substrate remains open.
